entries.originalLine: Because the ALB distributes the load across processes, the local in-memory counters remain independent. A single client can make up to 10 requests to Instance A and up to 10 requests to Instance B simultaneously, effectively doubling their allowance to 20 requests per minute without any instance-level rate limits triggering. In-memory storage completely fails to coordinate and enforce the global 10-request limit.
